rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 8 (sensors at y 0.06, base_speed 1.2, kp 1.5, kd 0.6) is the best raced design at 686.6. Oval and s-bend finished 20 of 20, and slalom progress rose from 0.33 to 0.40 when the sensors moved forward. Iteration 9 raised base_speed to 1.4 and scored lower (639.2). Oval time fell from 2.00 s to 1.79 s, but s-bend finishes dropped to 17 of 20 with 3 off-track ends. Each lost finish costs about 900 points, far more than the time term gains, and the revert rule (finishes below 18 of 20) is met. The entityR1 feedback describes 1.4 as the untested candidate, but that step has now been raced, so it is rejected. Speed stays at 1.2. Slalom is still the bottleneck: it ends off track in 20 of 20 runs and has 1.15 line-loss events per run. Gain, line_loss and sensor-y changes have not fixed it. Across iterations 3 to 8, each kd increase (0.3 to 0.5 to 0.6) raised slalom progress (0.23 to 0.24 to 0.33 at y 0.04). The s-bend oscillation in iteration 8 was 0.31, which leaves room for one more damping step.

Change. From iteration 8, one value: controller.kd 0.6 to 0.7. Everything else is held at the iteration 8 values: sensors at y 0.06, x -0.03 to 0.03, size 0.016, kp 1.5, ki 0.02, base_speed 1.2, sensor_weights unchanged, line_loss last_direction.

Expected result. Slalom progress should rise above 0.40 and its line-loss events should fall slightly. Oval and s-bend should keep 20 of 20 finishes, with oscillation at or below about 0.35.

Risks and fallback. kd 0.7 may amplify sensor noise, and the 0.4 oscillation guard is close. If s-bend or oval finishes fall below 18 of 20, or steering_oscillation exceeds 0.4 on either track, revert kd to 0.6, which reproduces the iteration 8 best design (686.6). If slalom progress falls below 0.40 with the finishes held, kd 0.6 is also the better choice.

Hypotheses. H1: slalom overshoot at direction changes is still limited by damping, so kd 0.7 raises slalom progress. H2: kd 0.7 keeps s-bend oscillation below 0.4 at speed 1.2. Measurements: per-track completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, and noise_robustness, so the kd effect can be separated from the track results.
